text:
sophie: FYI customer ticket #C-9821 — their Llama-2-13B quantized endpoint (int8/calib) is showing ~2x p95 vs fp16 and some generation quality drift. They're on Dedicated and reported this started after last week's rollout. https://support.redwood.ai/t/C-9821

ajay: Thanks. Can you paste the exact endpoint config + sample inputs? we'll try to repro.

sophie: Config: model: llama-2-13b, variant: int8-calib-v3, route_policy: auto, batching: dynamic, batch_multiplier: 4. Sample: short queries (instruction style, avg tokens out 60). Ticket includes request_id=rcp-4492.

tara: I ran a quick smoke on staging with similar short queries. Repro: p95_int8=420ms, p95_fp16=210ms. Interesting: int8 avg tokens/sec lower even on same GPU.

ajay: Can you share profiler traces? nvtx/flamegraphs?

tara: Pasting trimmed perf log below:
```
# perf top like trace
kernel: quant_gemm_int8    time: 38%  (many small launches)
kernel: fp16_gemm         time: 21%
kernel: calib_collect     time: 12%  (synchronous, CPU->GPU copies)
kernel: kv_fetch          time: 8%
others: 21%
```
Flamegraph: https://internal.redwood.ai/fg/1925/rcp-4492 (private)

mike: Calibration spike looks suspicious. Our int8 variant does a post-load per-layer histogram sweep on first inferences to compute scale/zero points when using per-channel dynamic calibration. If that runs inline it can introduce extra device memcopies and kernel launches for short requests.

sam: Also seeing that kernel selector picked a small-block int8 GEMM for seq_len<=32 which has worse kernel-launch overhead, especially when batch sizes are 1-4. For short instruction queries batching heuristics don't accumulate enough.

ajay: So two contributors: inline calibration overhead + kernel selection that favors int8 microkernels at short sequence lengths. That matches the perf numbers.

tara: I dug into logs: calibration runs only on cold start or when model variant marked "needs_calib=true". For this customer their dedicated instance got restarted during the rollout window which triggered calibration on their first traffic bursts. Calib_work unit shows sequential per-layer passes.

mike: Quick mitigation options:
- route this customer to fp16 variant until we fix heuristics
- enable async calibration background thread (short-term patch)
- bump batch_multiplier to 8 so batching >= kernel sweet spot
- add warmup traffic to pre-run calibration on deploys

ajay: Short-term action: 1) CS to ask customer to switch to fp16 for critical paths; 2) infra to enable temporary routing override for customer on dedicated; 3) eng to prepare hotfix to run calibration async. Who owns what?

sophie: I can message customer with proposed temporary switch to fp16. I'll include perf numbers and an estimate: p95 improvement ~2x.

mike: I'll open a routing override: PR for routing policy -> customer_id C-9821, prefer_variant: fp16-locked. ETA 30m.

ajay: I'll prototype an async calibration patch. Plan: spawn a single calibration worker per model instance that pulls layer tasks from queue and runs them with low-priority stream. That avoids blocking the main inference stream. If we can't land in time, we can disable calib on startup for these customers.

tara: For the medium term we should change kernel selector thresholds: prefer fused fp16 path for seq_len<=64 when batch<=4 unless batch_multiplier suggests we will gather more. Also add telemetry tag so we can catch when int8 path underperforms.

sam: Ops note: KV-cache miss pattern also amplified overhead. Calibration copies allocate temp buffers which push eviction heuristics and force extra kv_copy in/out. Adding pre-warm will reduce that.

ajay: Repro steps saved in the incident doc:
1) Run workload: 1000 short prompts, concurrency=2, batch_multiplier=4
2) Capture nvprof/nvtx, look for calib_collect + quant_gemm_int8 frequent small launches
3) Toggle variant to fp16 and re-run to compare
Commands:```bash
# repro run
python tools/bench_endpoint.py --model llama-2-13b --variant int8-calib-v3 --qps 50 --concurrency 2 --num-reqs 1000 > int8.log
python tools/bench_endpoint.py --variant fp16 --same > fp16.log
# perf
python tools/attach_profiler.py --pid <endpoint_pid> --out trace.nvtx
```

mike: PRs/links:
- routing override: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/842
- async-calib POC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1219 (draft)

sophie: Messaging to customer (draft):
"We investigated and found the quantized variant runs a synchronous calibration pass on cold start which can briefly increase latency for short queries. As a temporary mitigation we can switch your endpoint to the fp16 variant which gives ~2x lower p95 for short prompts. We can also pre-warm calibration for you after deployments so this doesn't affect production. Which would you prefer?" :thumbsup: :eyes:

ajay: I'll add telemetry alert to detect when int8 p95 > fp16 p95 * 1.3 for 15m.

tara: Follow-ups:
- (mike) routing override applied ✅ at 1925001260
- (sophie) customer notified at 1925001272, they accepted fp16 fallback
- (ajay) async-calib draft posted, perf baseline shows p95_int8 after async < 1.1 * p95_fp16 for our staging short-query workload

sophie: Customer response: "Switch to fp16 now, please. Keep us posted on the async fix as we want quant in future."

ajay: Next steps: land async-calib, tune kernel selector thresholds, add warmup hooks for dedicated restarts, and update runbooks. I'll file engineering tasks.

ops-bot: Incident C-9821 updated: status -> mitigated (fp16 fallback). Links: routing PR, runtime PR draft.

mike: Thanks all. I'll follow up with a short postmortem and a suggested comms template for CS to use for similar cases.

sophie: tagging for follow-up: @ajay @mike @tara @sam.
